newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia worried about defence as army lacks cash.
newsitem.headline: Russia worried about defence as army lacks cash.

text.p: Russian military chiefs are worried that cash shortages are damaging defence capabilities but a senior official said he did not think an army mutiny likely.
"The army is the army. There will be no mutinies unless they are specially prepared," Defence Council Secretary Yuri Baturin told NTV commercial television on Friday.
Baturin, speaking after the first meeting of a new Defence Council, did not elaborate but he was apparently referring to the possibility of someone inciting the army to revolt.
Russian security chief Alexander Lebed said last week that the army could be hit by revolts as a result of unpaid wages.

The outspoken Lebed, an ex-paratroop general, did not attend the closed-door session of the Defence Council, a body comprising top state, defence and security officials set up by President Boris Yeltsin in July.
The 65-year-old president on Thursday told the government to resolve cash problems in the army, where many soldiers have not been paid for months.
"Russia must have a modern and professional army," Yeltsin said in a radio address from the Central Clinical Hospital, where he is getting ready for heart surgery.

Baturin played down talk of a rift with Lebed, whose office said he did not attend the Defence Council meeting because he was working on a peace agreement reached on Thursday between Moscow and Chechen separatist leaders.

Lebed makes no secret of his presidential ambitions and Yeltsin's creation of the Defence Council was widely regarded as an attempt to establish a counterweight to another Kremlin body -- the Security Council -- of which Lebed is secretary.

The functions of the two bodies overlap. These include military reform, the defence budget and key military-political issues such as Russia's response to the planned eastward expansion of the West's NATO alliance.

"The Defence Council is ready to work constructively with the Security Council," Baturin said, adding that they might cooperate on a new military doctrine. But he said he had not been in contact with Lebed since the end of July.

The Defence Council meeting, chaired by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, examined ways of reorganising the armed forces. Government officials said there were too many generals and too much bureaucracy.

Some changes have already been made. The Defence Ministry said on Friday that Yeltsin had sacked several senior generals and Russian media said the move showed new minister Igor Rodionov, appointed in July, was ready for action.

Rodionov has announced plans to reduce the army to 1.2 million from about 1.5 million men. Baturin said the least effective units would be disbanded but he was worried that the ranks could be thinned badly as a result of the cash squeeze.
"I am concerned about a mass resignation of officers," he said. "This will affect the military capability of the country."

Baturin said there were differences at Friday's meeting over the strategy for developing the armed forces. Future policies would partly depend on relations with NATO, whose planned expansion Moscow sees as a threat to its security, he said.

Lebed is due to travel to NATO headquarters in Brussels this weekend. It will be the first time he has travelled to the West. He has said in the past that he knew too many military secrets to be allowed to travel.
